before_tex:
Industrial monitoring covers things like fault detection, checking the physical condition of a
system, assessing manufacturing quality and confirming that a robot has completed its task. The
traditional approach is to use single sensor readings and engineered features to characterise the
system's behaviour. Learned representations take this further by utilising data from images, sound
and sensor sequences. Multimodal learning looks at how information from different modalities can be
combined to assist with a common prediction task
\citep{Baltrusaitis2019Multimodal,Huo2022Multisensor,Thoduka2024Handover}.
after_tex:
Industrial monitoring covers tasks such as fault detection, checking a system's physical condition,
assessing manufacturing quality, and confirming that a robot has completed its task. The traditional
approach uses single sensor readings and engineered features to characterise the system's behaviour.
Learned representations take this further by utilising data from images, sound and sensor sequences.
Multimodal learning examines how information from different modalities can be combined to support a
common prediction task \citep{Baltrusaitis2019Multimodal,Huo2022Multisensor,Thoduka2024Handover}.

before_tex:
The literature touches on a number of related areas of research: traditional feature engineering,
the use of pre-trained representations, modelling over time, feature combination, prediction fusion
and adaptive methods (where the method can adapt to the context). They differ in terms of the
information they require, their computational cost, the level of supervision they need and their
sensitivity to the quality of the input.
after_tex:
The literature touches on several related areas of research: traditional feature engineering, the
use of pre-trained representations, modelling over time, feature combination, prediction fusion, and
adaptive methods (where the method can adapt to the context). They differ in the information they
require, their computational cost, the level of supervision they need, and their sensitivity to
input quality.

before_tex:
Industrial and robotic monitoring provides a platform on which to compare these approaches as the
process can be monitored via a number of different modalities (cameras, acoustic sensors, machine
sensors, etc.). Cameras will obviously provide a view of the visible process, whereas the acoustic
and machine sensors provide information which is not visible. The benefit of combining data is
highly dependent on the information that each modality retains, the particular prediction that
you're trying to make and the test conditions of the system
\citep{Wang2020What,Hua2026Weld,Goodarzi2023Deep}. Simply increasing the amount of data does not
necessarily lead to better predictions.
after_tex:
Industrial and robotic monitoring provides a platform on which to compare these approaches as the
process can be monitored via a number of different modalities (cameras, acoustic sensors, machine
sensors, etc.). Cameras will obviously provide a view of the visible process, whereas the acoustic
and machine sensors provide information which is not visible. The benefit of combining data depends
heavily on what each modality retains, the specific prediction you're trying to make, and the
system's test conditions \citep{Wang2020What,Hua2026Weld,Goodarzi2023Deep}. Simply increasing the
amount of data does not necessarily lead to better predictions.

before_tex:
Robotic welding is the principal driver of this thesis. The work on welding using visual and
acoustic data has shown that multimodal integration can lead to improved prediction performance, but
also that in some cases the addition of a further modality provides no benefit at all
\citep{P003,Hua2026Weld}. The Intel Welding audit documented prior examination of the proposed
assessment population, so an independent assessment of weld quality was not possible on that
population (see Chapter~\ref{ch:introduction}). The review therefore addresses the more general
architectural question across a range of industrial and robotic monitoring tasks: how physical
measurements, visual data and sensor data can be combined in order to assess system condition and
task outcome.
after_tex:

before_tex:
The review looks at the industrial fusion claims via the methodologies, the comparison tables and
the experimental results of the papers. It's very much focused on the link between the proposed
architecture, the physical observations that are actually available, the prediction target and the
assessment protocol.
after_tex:
The review examines industrial fusion claims through the methodologies, comparison tables, and
experimental results of the papers. It focuses on the link between the proposed architecture, the
available physical observations, the prediction target, and the assessment protocol.

before_tex:
A research gap is defined as a comparison that the existing body of scientific evidence does not
address for a given target, input set and assessment population. The ability to identify such a gap
will of course depend on the search strategy and the amount of published literature that is
available.
after_tex:
A research gap is defined as a comparison that the existing body of scientific evidence does not
address for a given target, input set and assessment population. The ability to identify such a gap
will, of course, depend on the search strategy and the amount of published literature available.

before_tex:
The representation theme is about what is being observed, what transformations are being applied and
whether the representation retains the information that is relevant to the task at hand. The fusion
theme is about whether the addition of further inputs leads to an improvement in performance on a
standard prediction task when compared to a set of plausible single input references.
after_tex:
The representation theme concerns what is being observed, what transformations are being applied,
and whether the representation retains the information relevant to the task at hand. The fusion
theme is about whether adding further inputs improves performance on a standard prediction task
compared with a set of plausible single-input references.

before_tex:
The review makes a clear distinction between two objectives which are often confused. Training with
multiple modalities in order to deploy a single input model is a privileged training scenario.
Combining multiple available inputs at deployment is a multimodal inference problem. Cross-modal
distillation and reconstruction link the two objectives but the acquisition assumptions are very
different.
after_tex:
The review clearly distinguishes between two objectives that are often confused. Training with
multiple modalities to deploy a single-input model is a privileged training scenario. Combining
multiple available inputs at deployment is a multimodal inference problem. Cross-modal distillation
and reconstruction link the two objectives but the acquisition assumptions are very different.
